Elon‍ Musk’s Twitter Takeover: A Deep Dive into His ‌First Two Weeks In the digital age, few figures have captivated the public’s attention as much as Elon Musk . His​ foray into the world‍ of social media, ⁢especially Twitter, has ‌been nothing‍ short of seismic. Within his first two weeks on ​the platform, Musk’s​ interactions have sparked conversations, controversies, and a flurry of memes.Let’s delve into⁣ the key moments and themes ‌that have defined this period.
The Meme Master Musk’s Twitter presence is heavily influenced by his interactions with various meme accounts. One such account is DOGE , which lists several of Musk’s aides.when an account published this​ list, musk responded sternly, “You have committed a crime,” leading to the account’s removal‌ by Twitter. This incident underscores Musk’s strict stance‌ on privacy ⁢and the influence he wields on the platform.
another notable account is Amuse , which boasts over 530,000 followers. musk reposted or quote-tweeted it more than 20 times in his first 14 days. ‌Similarly, Rabbit Hole , with over 978,000 followers, saw Musk repost or reply‌ to its ‍content more than ⁤30 times in the same period. ⁢These interactions highlight Musk’s penchant for engaging with and‌ trending‌ content.
The Dogecoin Dilemma Musk’s tweets ‍about Dogecoin (DOGE) have been a recurring theme. When an account published a list of several of musk’s aides working under ‌DOGE,⁢ Musk replied, “You have committed a crime,” leading to the account’s removal by Twitter. This incident underscores Musk’s strict stance on privacy and the influence he wields on the platform.
The Straight Arm Controversy One‍ of the most talked-about moments was​ Musk’s speech to Trump supporters following the presidential inauguration. At the end⁣ of his speech, Musk ‌made a gesture that several media organizations described ⁢as a fascist or “Roman” salute.‌ Musk later dismissed these ‍claims,⁢ stating, “It was astonishing⁣ how insanely⁤ hard legacy media tried to cancel‌ me for saying ‘my heart goes⁣ out to you’⁢ and moving my hand from my⁣ heart to ⁢the audience. this deception will just be another nail in the ⁣coffin of ‌legacy media.”
Media ⁣and Misleading claims Musk ‍has been vocal about his criticisms of mainstream media. He has amplified tweets criticizing outlets​ like Politico, BBC, NPR, and ​CBS, often⁢ sharing misleading claims. For ‍instance, he⁢ echoed claims that⁣ “billions‍ of dollars” had been paid to “fake news” for positive coverage, with $8m allegedly going to Politico. Politico’s leadership ‌denied these allegations,​ stating that the outlet “has never been⁤ a ⁣beneficiary of government programs or subsidies -⁢ not one cent, ever.”
European Focus Musk’s tweets have⁣ also turned ⁤their focus to European media and issues. ⁢He frequently‌ posted variations of the message ‘MEGA – Make Europe Great Again.’ Often, he amplified an account‌ linked to‍ a cryptocurrency scam called⁢ InevitableWest . On February 5,Musk reposted content from this account claiming that no‌ European leaders had mentioned a shooting in a Swedish education facility where 10 people were killed. By that⁣ point, multiple​ European leaders‌ had issued statements condemning​ the shooting.

The video captures the terrifying moments outside, where shots can ‌be heard, and⁢ a​ person shouts, “You‌ will leave Europe!” This video, which has been seen 50 million times and retweeted by 46,000 accounts, was reposted by​ Musk with the comment‍ “Wow.” The video’s context and the subsequent‍ reactions have raised concerns about ​the spread of inflammatory content.

His support for the UK-based party AfD and⁣ his⁢ encouragement for followers ​to vote for them have further ⁢fueled debates‍ about ​his influence. Musk’s actions have ‍raised questions about the potential conflicts of ⁣interest, especially considering his companies’ numerous contracts with US government agencies.
